english: Between the houses there is a park.
tip: между (mezhdu = between) takes the instrumental, so дом (dom = house) becomes домами (damami = houses) in the plural.

english: The ball rolled under the bed.
tip: For motion to a spot, под (pod = under) switches to the accusative: под кровать (pod kravat = under the bed).

english: The grown-up children left.
tip: Past active participles end in -ший: выросшие дети (vyrosshie deti = the grown-up children), from вырасти (vyrasti = to grow up).

english: In spring the birds return.
tip: Seasons take the bare instrumental to mean in that season, no preposition: весной (vesnoy = in spring), from весна (vesna = spring).

english: They say he left.
tip: говорят, что (gavaryat, chto = they say that) is an impersonal 3rd-plural verb, no subject needed, reading as it is said.

english: He skipped class.
tip: с (s) plus genitive means off or from a place or event: сбежал с урока (sbezhal s uroka = ran off from class), урок (urok) going to урока.

english: She flew over the ocean.
tip: The prefix пере- (pere-) on a motion verb means across: перелетела (pereletela = flew across) через океан (cherez akean = over the ocean).

english: The bored child wants to play.
tip: Present active participles end in -щий: скучающий ребёнок (skuchayushchiy rebyonok = the bored child), from скучать (skuchat = to be bored).

english: In half a year he will return.
tip: через (cherez) plus accusative counts time from now: через полгода (cherez palgoda = in half a year), meaning after that span.

english: The broken chair needs to be fixed.
tip: Past passive participles end in -нный and act as adjectives: сломанный стул (slomannyy stul = broken chair), from сломать (slamat = to break).

english: In winter we ski.
tip: кататься на (katatsya na) plus prepositional means to go doing a sport: катаемся на лыжах (kataemsya na lyzhah = we ski).

english: On Thursday I have an exam.
tip: Days of the week take в plus accusative: в четверг (v chetverg = on Thursday), четверг unchanged as an inanimate noun.

english: Once we went to the sea.
tip: Some destinations take на plus accusative, not в (v): поехали на море (paehali na more = went to the sea).

english: He said that he would come tomorrow.
tip: Russian keeps the original tense in reported speech: сказал, что придёт (skazal, chto pridyot = said he will come), no backshift to would.

target: Каждый день я хожу на работу.
english: Every day I go to work.
tip: For a repeated trip use ходить (hadit), not one-way идти (idti): каждый день я хожу (kazhdyy den ya hazhu = every day I go).

target: На следующей неделе у нас праздник.
english: Next week we have a celebration.
tip: Weeks take на plus prepositional, not в (v): на следующей неделе (na sleduyushchey nedele = next week).

target: Он попросил, чтобы я помог ему.
english: He asked me to help him.
tip: After a request, чтобы takes a past-form verb: попросил, чтобы я помог (paprasil, chtoby ya pamog = asked that I help).

target: Мама спросила, сделал ли я уроки.
english: Mom asked if I had done my homework.
tip: For an embedded yes/no question use ли after the key word: сделал ли я (sdelal li ya = whether I did), no if word needed.

target: Из года в год мы приезжаем сюда.
english: Year after year we come here.
tip: из ... в ... expresses repetition: из года в год (iz goda v god = year after year), год appearing first in genitive, then accusative.

target: В последний раз мы виделись в мае.
english: The last time we saw each other was in May.
tip: Months take в plus prepositional: в мае (v maye = in May), from май (may = May).

target: Письмо было отправлено по электронной почте вчера вечером.
english: The letter was sent by email yesterday evening.
tip: Past passive uses было plus a short participle: письмо было отправлено (pismo bylo atpravleno = the letter was sent).

english: We drove past the park.
tip: мимо (mimo = past) takes the genitive: проехали мимо парка (praehali mimo parka = drove past the park), парк (park) becoming парка.

english: The plane flew over the city.
tip: над (nad = over) takes the instrumental: пролетел над городом (praletel nad gorodom = flew over the city), город (gorod) becoming городом.

english: With each day it gets warmer.
tip: с plus instrumental means with: с каждым днём (s kazhdym dnyom = with each day), день (den) becoming днём.

english: While reading a book, he drank tea.
tip: An -я gerund shows a simultaneous action by the same subject: читая книгу (chitaya knigu = while reading a book), from читать (chitat = to read).

target: Никто не сказал, что будет легко.
english: Nobody said it would be easy.
tip: A negative word still needs не on the verb: никто не сказал (nikto ne skazal = nobody said), the double negative is required.

target: В прошлом году я был в Париже.
english: Last year I was in Paris.
tip: Years take в plus prepositional: в прошлом году (v proshlom gadu = last year), год (god) taking the special locative ending году.

english: The smiling woman looks friendly.
tip: улыбающаяся (ulybayushchayasya = smiling) is a participle used like an adjective, agreeing with женщина (zhenshchina = woman) in gender and case.

english: We said that we agreed.
tip: Russian always puts a comma before что (chto = that) in reported speech: сказали, что согласны (skazali, chto saglasny = said that we agree).

english: The opened window lets in air.
tip: открытое (atkrytoe = opened) is a past passive participle used like an adjective, agreeing with окно (akno = window).
